# Pocket TTS, phoneme input, 14 languages

One [Pocket TTS](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/pocket-tts) model (24-layer FlowLM + Mimi, 24 kHz, voice cloning
from a few seconds of audio) that reads **IPA with word stress** instead of spelling, fine-tuned for **Italian,
Spanish, French, German, English, Dutch, Portuguese, Polish, Czech, Russian, Turkish, Estonian, Hindi and Korean**.
Because the input is phonemes, one model serves every language, with no per-language weights to swap.

It is the phoneme talker of the **hybrid-multi** profile of [mynah-s2s](https://github.com/mynah-org/mynah-s2s)
(`make hybrid-multi-setup TALKER=phonemes && make hybrid-multi TALKER=phonemes`; the default talker of that profile is
the per-language [Pocket TTS deltas](https://huggingface.co/gabrione/pocket-tts-deltas)); the recipe, the G2P front
end and the evaluation tools are there (`labs/phoneme_tts/`).

## Files

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `model.safetensors` | the weights (pocket-tts inference format: `flow_lm.*`, `mimi.*`) |
| `model.yaml` | the pocket-tts model config |
| `tokenizer.json` | the IPA SentencePiece tokenizer (4000 pieces, byte fallback) |
| `manifest.json` | languages, G2P, training step, checksums |
| `lexicon/<lang>.tsv` | word -> IPA tables (`word<TAB>ipa`, with stress) made with the training G2P, so no G2P program is needed at serving time |

## Input: IPA words with stress marks

The model reads IPA words separated by spaces, without punctuation, **with the stress marks** `ˈ ˌ` that espeak-ng
writes, affricates with tie bars (`t͡ʃ d͡ʒ t͡s d͡z`). The G2P is part of the model: use the same one.

| lang | G2P |
|---|---|
| all 14 | espeak-ng **1.51** through phonemizer 3.6.0, `with_stress=True`, stress kept (`ipa_words.py` in mynah-s2s, `keep_stress=True`) |

Numbers must be written as words before the G2P (no number normaliser inside). espeak-ng picks one reading for
homographs.

**Word tables.** Training phonemized every word on its own, so a table of words made with the same conversion gives
exactly the training IPA. `lexicon/` holds one table per language: the words of the training transcripts, FLEURS,
the mynah-s2s agent's replies, the 300,000 most frequent words of [wordfreq](https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq)
(not available for Estonian; fewer for Turkish, Hindi and Korean), the numbers 0 to 10,000 and the letters A to Z,
each through espeak-ng 1.51 as above (about 310,000 words for the large languages, 35,000 to 80,000 for et, tr, hi,
ko). mynah-s2s reads them in the engine's own process (`hybrid/tts/phonemes/frontend.py`, `LexiconG2P`): a missing
word is read from its parts when it is hyphenated or a code (letters spelled, numbers read).

## Evaluation

30 FLEURS test sentences per language, transcribed by Omni ASR CTC 3B v2. The gap is the WER of the synthetic
speech minus the WER of the real recordings of the same sentences (what the talker loses). "Fixed voice": one
reference voice per language for all sentences; "cloned": 5 s of another speaker of the test set.

| | it | es | fr | de | en | nl | pt | pl | cs | ru | tr | et | hi | ko |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| real recordings WER | .029 | .031 | .107 | .051 | .090 | .081 | .052 | .092 | .085 | .098 | .129 | .125 | .173 | .209 |
| gap, fixed voice | .035 | .020 | .002 | .033 | .008 | .056 | .078 | .036 | −.002 | .039 | .060 | .058 | .058 | .199 |
| gap, cloned voice | .037 | .044 | .051 | .041 | .193 | .136 | .079 | .126 | .092 | .075 | .097 | .200 | .016 | .137 |

Word stress was checked by ear in Italian on sentences dense in stress pairs (*nemici*, *predominano*, *àncora* /
*ancóra*, *prìncipi* / *princìpi*); the previous version without stress in the input got several of them wrong.

Long texts: speak them sentence by sentence (as a voice engine does); one-shot texts much longer than the training
clips (~30 s) degrade.

## Training

- Base: `kyutai/pocket-tts` English 24-layer, fine-tuned on IPA: first the eight MLS languages, then six more, then
  two stages with word stress in the input; 15000 steps in total, batch 32, bf16, LSD flow loss.
- Data: [MLS](https://www.openslr.org/94/) (it, es, fr, de, en, nl, pt, pl), [FLEURS](https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/fleurs)
  train (all 14), Common Voice 17 (cs, ru, tr, et); word timestamps by forced alignment with Omni ASR CTC; at most
  15 minutes per speaker.
- Trainer: Kyutai's Pocket TTS training code (MIT), as distributed in AfriSpeech/africa-tts (MIT).

## Licences and attribution

- Weights: **CC-BY-4.0**, a derivative of [kyutai/pocket-tts](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/pocket-tts) (CC-BY-4.0,
  Kyutai).
- Training data: MLS (CC-BY-4.0), FLEURS (CC-BY-4.0), Common Voice 17 (CC0-1.0).
- `tokenizer.json`: the IPA tokenizer of [AfriSpeech/africa-tts](https://github.com/AfriSpeech/africa-tts) (MIT,
  Copyright (c) 2026 AfriSpeech / Ghana NLP).
- `lexicon/`: **CC-BY-SA-4.0**. The word lists include [wordfreq](https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq)'s data
  (CC-BY-SA-4.0, Robyn Speer and contributors); the pronunciations are espeak-ng 1.51's output.
- espeak-ng and phonemizer (GPL-3.0) are not included; install them yourself only to make new tables or to use
  another G2P.
- No voice is distributed here; bring your own reference audio, with the speaker's consent.

## Limitations

- Korean has the largest gap; Estonian, English and Dutch lose most with cloned voices.
- No punctuation in the input, so no question intonation.
- Stress comes from espeak-ng's dictionary and rules: where espeak-ng is wrong, the model is too.
